newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium demand to show strong growth to 99-Bird.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium demand to show strong growth to 99-Bird.

text.p: Aluminium consumption will rise more rapidly than economic activity between 1997 and 1999, growing by 4.5-5.75 percent per year, industry specialists Anthony Bird Associates said.
"But the coming rise in aluminium prices will destroy this competitive edge. Thus consumption will be virtually stagnant in 2000," Bird said in its latest quarterly analysis.
Supply should be able to keep up with demand in the medium term, but by 1999 the availability of aluminium will become difficult, the report said.
"Aluminium companies have been under-investing for many years and it now seems inevitable that the supply situation will become very tight indeed, probably in 1999, perhaps earlier," it added.

"As to the exact date of the coming shortage, much depends on estimates of the size of the hidden metal stocks, and of how much metal can still be imported from Russia when that country's domestic demand recovers," it said.
Aluminium prices were at a fair level currently, but they should start to anticipate the shortage in 1998 and rise very sharply in 1999.

"It is virtually impossible to predict how high prices might go in 2000. But the precedent of 1988, when market conditions were very similar, suggests that the price spike could be very dramatic indeed," the report said.
By the second half of 2000, however, prices should weaken very rapidly.
